summary.title: Evolution of my role as a founder CTO
summary.one_liner: A first-person account of how a technical co-founder's CTO role shifted from hands-on coding to delegation and VP of Engineering-style work as RevenueCat grew from 2018 to 2021.
keywords: when to stop coding as cto
senior staff engineer vs engineering management
takeaways: The CTO role (architecture and code) and the VP of Engineering role (process and management) are different skill sets; most startups eventually hire externally for VPE.
Engineering breaking points often appear around 8 to 12 engineers, and founders may temporarily wear both CTO and VPE hats.
Stop coding and delegate when you become the bottleneck; delegation freed time to plan the future engineering organization.
Establish an on-call policy early, document known incident resolutions, and reduce the bus factor as the team grows.
Choose the role that is most impactful for the company at each stage, rather than only personal preference.
summary.summary: The author, co-founder and CTO of RevenueCat, reflects on how his responsibilities changed over the company's first three years, using yearly journal notes from 2018 to 2020 and plans for 2021. He frames the CTO versus VP of Engineering dilemma, discusses founder motivation and dopamine-driven preferences, and notes that team breaking points often come at 8 to 12 engineers. Each year is summarized with a team-size table, the main concerns of that period, and key learnings such as moving from de facto on-call to a rotation and stopping coding to delegate. The piece is a personal retrospective rather than a how-to, and it ends with a note that it will be updated yearly.
